title: Spectral completeness interpretation: nothing is missing from $\alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}$
html:
Remark. Spectral completeness interpretation: nothing is missing from \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}

The completeness theorem (completeness) and its corollary (uniqueness) establish the singlet channel as the unique one-dimensional invariant subspace of A \otimes A. It acts as the sole scalar exchange channel. The symmetric channel V_+ has R-rank \dim_q V_+ = [3]_q. It is the spin-1 irrep of \mathrm{SU}_q(2) and carries non-trivial spin. It cannot serve as a scalar gauge coupling.

The categorical R-matrix possesses a rank-2 endomorphism algebra over R. Plancherel completeness w_+ + w_- = 1 exhausts the Frobenius mass. No third channel exists. This guarantees no missing scalar coupling. Modulo force-carrier complexity normalisation (force-carrier uniqueness), the singlet weight w_- equals \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} (EM coupling projection).

Spectral collapse and confinement. The two-strand completeness theorem provides the n = 2 instance of spectral-sequence collapse (spectral collapse) and its confinement reading (confinement = collapse). The condition \mathrm{HH}^{\geq 1}(H_n(R, q)) = 0 collapses every non-central element at E_\infty. This leaves only Z(H_n(R, q)) = \bigoplus_\lambda R \cdot e_\lambda. At n = 2, the centre decomposes into two summands e_+, e_-. The singlet e_- forms the unique one-dimensional summand. The QCD analogue (confinement reading) asserts that non-central elements remain unobservable at E_\infty. This forces observables to factor through \pi_Z. The photon channel thus represents the unique colour-singlet projection at n = 2, with \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} as its Frobenius-pairing weight.

Specialisation. The categorical statement holds over R. Numerical evaluation fixes a ring map \iota \colon R \to \mathbb{R} satisfying q^{1/2} \mapsto q_0^{1/2} at q_0 = 1.109978595642739\ldots (muon pin, 16 dps). The completeness theorem is independent of \iota. It survives any specialisation to \mathbb{Q}_p or \mathbb{F}_\ell that admits the required units.
